hook: How many times does a V meet a wave?
caption:
JEE Main graph trick: how many solutions does |x| = cos x have? 🤔
Comment your answer BEFORE the reveal 👇

cos x keeps waving forever, so it looks like a lot. The 20-second method:
1️⃣ cos x is never above 1, so |x| = cos x needs −1 ≤ x ≤ 1
2️⃣ on the right, y = x climbs from 0 while cos x falls from 1: one crossing
3️⃣ both graphs are symmetric, so the left side gives one more

✅ Answer: 2 real solutions (x ≈ ±0.739)

Bound it first, then count. It cracks most "number of solutions" questions in JEE Main.

The 2-line method:
1️⃣ Take log base 10: compare 100·log 2 with 63·log 3
2️⃣ 100 × 0.3010 = 30.10 and 63 × 0.4771 = 30.06

✅ Answer: 2¹⁰⁰ > 3⁶³
Both have 31 digits, which is why it feels so close.

Compare the logs, not the numbers. It works for any "which power is bigger" question.

hook: Every cubic has one real root. How many here?
caption:
JEE Main: how many real roots does x³ − 3x + 1 = 0 have? 🤔
Comment A, B, C or D before the reveal 👇

The 20-second method:
1️⃣ Turning points: f′(x) = 3x² − 3 = 0 → x = ±1
2️⃣ f(−1) = 3 (above the axis) and f(1) = −1 (below the axis)
3️⃣ Up, down, up → the curve must cross the x-axis 3 times

✅ Answer: 3 real roots (≈ −1.88, 0.35, 1.53)

A maximum above the axis and a minimum below it always means three real roots.

reel: Largest rectangle inside a circle of radius r
caption:
JEE Main maxima: what's the biggest rectangle that fits inside a circle of radius r? 🤔
Comment A, B, C or D before the reveal 👇

The 20-second method:
1️⃣ Put a corner on the circle at angle θ
2️⃣ Width = 2r cos θ, height = 2r sin θ
3️⃣ Area = 4r² sin θ cos θ = 2r² sin 2θ, which peaks at θ = 45°

✅ Answer: a square, with area 2r²

Turn the shape into one angle, then maximise one trig function.

caption:
JEE Main limits: what does sin x / x approach as x → 0? 🤔
Comment A, B, C or D before the reveal 👇

The 20-second proof:
1️⃣ On the unit circle, three areas sit one inside the next: triangle, sector, triangle
2️⃣ That gives sin x < x < tan x
3️⃣ Divide by sin x: cos x < sin x / x < 1, and cos x → 1

✅ Answer: 1 (squeezed between cos x and 1)

This is the limit every trig-limit question in JEE is built on.

hook: Only two groups of order 4 exist
answer: Both (Z4 and the Klein four-group) are abelian
caption:
CSIR-NET Mathematics: how many groups of order 4 are there? 🤔
Comment A, B, C or D before the reveal 👇

The 20-second argument:
1️⃣ If some element has order 4, the group is cyclic: ℤ₄
2️⃣ If not, every element squares to the identity: the Klein four-group V₄
3️⃣ Both Cayley tables are symmetric across the diagonal, so ab = ba

✅ Answer: 2 groups (up to isomorphism), and both are abelian

A quick check worth knowing for Part B and C: every group of order p² is abelian.

hook: A matrix with no real eigenvector
caption:
CSIR-NET Mathematics: which real vector stays on its own line after a 90° rotation? 🤔
Comment A, B, C or D before the reveal 👇

The 20-second argument:
1️⃣ A 90° rotation turns every nonzero vector off its own line
2️⃣ So there is no real eigenvector
3️⃣ A = [[0, −1], [1, 0]]: det(A − λI) = λ² + 1 = 0

✅ Answer: none. The eigenvalues are ±i

Geometry first, then the characteristic polynomial confirms it.

Probability puzzle: 3 doors, 1 car. You pick a door, the host opens a goat door. Should you switch? 🚪
Comment A, B, C or D before the reveal 👇

The 20-second reason:
1️⃣ Your first pick is right 1 time in 3
2️⃣ So 2 times in 3 the car is behind one of the other two doors
3️⃣ The host opens a goat door, and that whole 2/3 moves to the last door

✅ Answer: switch. You win 2/3 of the time

The Monty Hall problem: the best test of conditional probability intuition.

first_comment: Did you think it settles at 2? 👇
caption:
CSIR-NET Mathematics: does 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + … ever stop growing? 🤔
Comment A, B, C or D before the reveal 👇

The grouping proof:
1️⃣ 1/3 + 1/4 > 1/2
2️⃣ 1/5 + … + 1/8 > 1/2, and 1/9 + … + 1/16 > 1/2
3️⃣ Every block of terms adds at least 1/2, forever

✅ Answer: the harmonic series diverges

The terms go to 0, but that alone never proves convergence. (π²/6 is the sum of 1/n², not 1/n.)
